meta.title: Hot Days, Safe Days
meta.textType: functional: a school science text with headings, and a talk

paragraphs: On Tuesday, April twentieth, at two o'clock, Nurse Jill gave the Health Hour at the town library. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat at a long table. Each child had a handout and a water bottle. It was a warm afternoon, so the doors of the library were open. Behind Nurse Jill stood a big poster of a red heart. "Your heart works hard all day," she said. "Do you know how to look after it?" "First, we will read the handout."

The handout had five headings. Nurse Jill read them to the children. The first was "Your heart and your blood." The second was "Why running makes your heart go faster." The third was "Why we sweat." The fourth was "Drink water and rest in the shade." The last was "Look after yourself." Under the first heading, the handout said, "The heart is a strong muscle." "Blood is pushed around your body all day and all night." "It brings food and air to every part of your body."

Next, Nurse Jill showed the children how to find a pulse. "Put two fingers on the inside of your wrist," she said. "Feel your pulse, and count it for fifteen seconds." Lily held two fingers on her wrist and looked at the wall clock. Mia held a pencil over a table of numbers, and May held her water bottle. Lily counted eighteen beats while she sat. "Eighteen beats in fifteen seconds is a normal pulse for a child," said Nurse Jill. Then the children ran on the spot for one minute. Lily stopped and counted again. Leo was still running behind her with a big smile. "Thirty beats!" said Lily. Mia wrote thirty in the table next to eighteen.

"Running makes your heart go fast," said Nurse Jill. "This is because your body needs more blood." "Running is exercise." "Exercise is good for your health." "A healthy heart is a strong heart." Then she pointed at the third heading. "Sweat is made when your body gets too hot." "It helps your body to stay cool." "So a wet shirt after exercise is normal."

Under the fourth heading, the handout said, "On a hot day, a child may feel tired or dizzy." "Then rest in the shade and drink some water." Leo sat down and drank from his bottle. "Is cold water better than warm water?" he asked. "A drink that is not too cold may be better in the heat," answered Nurse Jill.

Last, Nurse Jill read the fifth heading, "Look after yourself." "Drink water, rest in the shade, and tell an adult if you feel bad," she said. May wrote the five headings in her notebook. Lily looked at the table of numbers and smiled. "My heart worked very hard today," she said. "My heart is fast and my shirt is wet, but I am healthy," said Leo.
text.summary: At the library's Health Hour, Nurse Jill teaches the children about the heart, the pulse, and sweat. The children count their pulse before and after running on the spot, and they learn how to stay safe on a hot day.
